incidents.victim: Meta (Instagram) — Obama White House & US Space Force accounts
incidents.vector: Pro-Iran actors abused Meta's AI customer-support bot to add an attacker-controlled email to target accounts and trigger a password-reset code, bypassing normal account-recovery controls.
incidents.impact: The Obama White House and the Chief Master Sergeant of the US Space Force Instagram accounts were defaced with pro-Iranian images and messages; Meta pushed an emergency patch and said no back-end database was breached. Hijacked short-form usernames were reportedly resold.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a flaw in a smart contract that moves assets between the Ethereum and Cosmos chains.
incidents.impact: Roughly $5.4 million in crypto drained from the bridge; the company halted trading over the weekend to investigate.

incidents.vector: Phishing compromise of a single employee account gave access to a limited portion of Carnival's IT environment in April; the attacker then copied personal data over the following weeks.
incidents.impact: Carnival confirmed roughly 6 million individuals had names, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, driver's license numbers and passport numbers exposed across its brands (Princess, Holland America, Cunard, Costa). The attacker posted 8.7 million records on its leak site after a failed extortion attempt.

incidents.vector: Attackers injected malicious GitHub Actions workflows via 5,700+ commits pushed on May 18, designed to harvest CI/CD secrets, cloud credentials and tokens during pipeline runs.
incidents.impact: More than 5,500 public repositories were back-doored, exposing API keys, cloud-provider credentials (AWS, GCP, Azure), SSH keys and registry tokens from development and deployment pipelines. CISA has issued mitigation guidance and urged organisations to rotate all CI/CD secrets.

incidents.vector: Reported intrusion by the Play ransomware crew with claimed exfiltration of sensitive financial documents from MyPillow's corporate network.
incidents.impact: Play has listed MyPillow on its data-leak site and is extorting the company. MyPillow has not yet confirmed the incident.

incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed; ShinyHunters listed Charter on its dark-web leak portal alongside dozens of other Salesforce-environment victims from the same campaign cluster.
incidents.impact: Charter confirmed a security breach after its name appeared on the leak site; scope and number of affected individuals were not disclosed.

incidents.victim: Lithuanian State Registry (real estate / cadastral data)
incidents.vector: Compromised credentials issued to other Lithuanian government agencies authorised to query the land and real-estate registry.
incidents.impact: Approximately 600,000 records exfiltrated, including property data, real names and cadastral information.

incidents.vector: Zero-day exploitation of CVE-2026-5426, a ViewState deserialisation flaw caused by hardcoded ASP.NET machineKey values shipped identically across customer deployments. Attackers crafted malicious ViewState payloads, deployed the BLUEBEAM (Godzilla) in-memory web shell, then tampered with site JavaScript to push fake "security plugins" that ultimately delivered Cobalt Strike BEACON to visitors.
incidents.impact: Mandiant responded to at least one compromise of a Japanese organisation; any internet-facing KnowledgeDeliver instance using the vendor default machineKey is exposed until keys are rotated. End-user workstations were infected with a Cobalt Strike implant uniquely keyed to the targeted organisation.

incidents.vector: Unprotected cloud server with no password authentication left publicly exposed for at least a week.
incidents.impact: More than 3.4 million scanned images exposed, including driver's licenses and legal and financial documents tied to inmates and their families. Server has since been secured.

incidents.victim: Stark Industries / MIRhosting / WorkTitans infrastructure (Russian cyber-ops staging)
incidents.vector: Dutch financial-crime agency FIOD executed sanctions-violation arrests of the two co-owners of MIRhosting and WorkTitans (the surviving connectivity behind EU-sanctioned PQHosting/Stark Industries) and raided data centres in Dronten and Schiphol-Rijk.
incidents.impact: Dutch authorities seized more than 800 servers used to launch DDoS attacks, run proxy and anonymity services, and stage Russia-linked influence and disinformation operations — including pro-Russian attacks on Danish government bodies during the November 2025 municipal elections. Customer data on the seized servers was lost.

incidents.victim: US and Israeli targets (Stryker, FBI Director Kash Patel, USMC, county governments, Israeli nuclear and government entities)
incidents.vector: MOIS-linked Handala persona conducting hack-and-leak operations, wiper deployments and ransomware-style intrusions, with claimed solicitation of physical attacks (assassinations, espionage, sabotage) against US and Israeli personnel through the new Handala Popular Resistance Front and three associated influence networks.
incidents.impact: Recorded Future Insikt Group attributes a surge of US-targeted operations since the start of the Iran War to MOIS under the Handala brand, including data leaks tied to US medical-device maker Stryker, FBI Director Kash Patel, US Marine Corps personnel and US county governments. The brand is now being used to recruit and coordinate physical-threat operations against US and Israeli law-enforcement, military, intelligence, energy, transportation and research personnel.

incidents.victim: Technology-sector entities in the US, Israel, UAE and additional Middle Eastern targets
incidents.vector: Tailored spear-phishing impersonating global air carriers, hiring portals and video-conferencing software, leveraging DLL sideloading and AppDomainManager hijacking to disable .NET security and deploy MiniUpdate and MiniJunk V2 remote-access trojans.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 confirmed six new RAT variants deployed between mid-February and mid-April 2026 against US, Israeli, UAE and other Middle Eastern targets, with each campaign using a dedicated set of Azure-hosted command-and-control domains to maintain operational resilience. Timing aligns with the regional conflict that began February 28, 2026.

incidents.victim: US water, energy and municipal critical infrastructure
incidents.vector: Targeting internet-exposed Rockwell Automation, Allen-Bradley and Israeli-made Unitronics Vision Series programmable logic controllers with default or weak credentials.
incidents.impact: CISA joint advisory AA26-097A confirms an active, ongoing IRGC-affiliated campaign against US critical-infrastructure PLCs at water, energy and municipal sites. Unit 42 flags this as a primary risk to ancillary infrastructure during the 2026 FIFA World Cup tournament window.

incidents.vector: Unsecured Elasticsearch database left exposed to the internet for at least two months.
incidents.impact: Personal data on roughly 19 million customers — tied to WeChat accounts, including full names and phone numbers — was exposed. The server has been secured.

incidents.victim: Internet-of-Things device owners and DDoS targets (including US DoD address ranges)
incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of firewalled IoT devices (digital photo frames, web cameras) recruited into a global botnet, then rented to other criminals or used to launch volumetric DDoS attacks reaching nearly 30 Tbps.
incidents.impact: Ontario Provincial Police arrested 23-year-old Ottawa resident Jacob Butler ("Dort") on a US extradition warrant; US authorities and partners had already seized infrastructure for Kimwolf and three competing IoT botnets (Aisuru, JackSkid, Mossad) on March 19. Kimwolf issued over 25,000 attack commands and caused some victims more than $1M in losses each.

incidents.vector: Malicious version 18.95.0 of the Nx Console VS Code extension (poisoned via a prior Nx developer compromise and pushed through VS Code's automatic update mechanism) executed on a GitHub employee device, granting access to internal repositories. Now tracked as CVE-2026-48027 and added to CISA's KEV catalog.
incidents.impact: Approximately 3,800 internal GitHub repositories were exfiltrated; TeamPCP attempted to extort GitHub for $50,000 and threatened a free leak. GitHub says customer data was unaffected, contained the breach the same day and rotated critical credentials. Grafana confirmed it was hit via the same underlying TanStack supply-chain incident.

incidents.vector: Compromise of 7-Eleven systems used to store franchisee documents; consistent with ShinyHunters' broader Salesforce-environment targeting campaign.
incidents.impact: Names, addresses and Social Security numbers of an undisclosed number of franchise-related individuals were stolen. Breach reported to attorneys general in Maine, Vermont and Massachusetts; FBI has urged ShinyHunters victims not to pay.

incidents.victim: Government of the Northern Mariana Islands
incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed; suspected ransomware or destructive intrusion against territorial email infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Cyberattack disrupted email servers of the US territory's government and is expected to slow administrative operations.

incidents.vector: Not publicly disclosed; intrusions reportedly went undetected for a period before discovery.
incidents.impact: Compromised networks store the personal data of millions of Vietnamese citizens; investigation is underway.

incidents.victim: Microsoft Azure (abused) and downstream ransomware victims globally
incidents.vector: Fox Tempest stood up hundreds of Azure tenants and abused Microsoft Artifact Signing to issue short-lived fraudulent code-signing certificates, which ransomware affiliates used to sign Oyster, Lumma Stealer and Vidar binaries masquerading as AnyDesk, Teams, PuTTY and Webex.
incidents.impact: Microsoft Digital Crimes Unit obtained a court order, seized Fox Tempest's website, took hundreds of VMs offline and revoked over 1,000 fraudulent certificates. Ransomware affiliates linked to Rhysida, INC, Qilin and Akira had paid the service millions to sign malware that infected thousands of machines across the US, China, France and India.

incidents.victim: BlueSky users (account takeovers for disinformation amplification)
incidents.vector: Account takeovers of BlueSky users (method not disclosed) to post pro-Kremlin and anti-Ukraine propaganda.
incidents.impact: BlueSky has been forced to suspend hijacked accounts until owners can resecure them; campaign is attributed to the same Matryoshka network behind prior Russian influence ops in Armenia, Moldova, France and Germany.

incidents.attacker: No confirmed attacker — exposed credentials publicly available
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor intentionally disabled GitHub's push-protection and published a public "Private-CISA" GitHub profile containing plaintext AWS GovCloud keys, an RSA private key for a CISA-IT GitHub app, and credentials to dozens of internal CISA systems. The most sensitive secrets were committed in late April 2026.
incidents.impact: An attacker monitoring the GitHub event firehose could have read every CISA-IT repository, hijacked CI/CD pipelines, and modified branch protections, webhooks and deploy keys. More than a week after disclosure, CISA was still working to invalidate and rotate exposed credentials tied to other critical security technologies. Senators Hassan, Thompson and Ramirez are demanding answers; the leak occurred against the backdrop of CISA losing over a third of its workforce.
